title: Drainage basins & hydrographs
examples: How do we know what is entering the river?
What does the shape of the hydrograph tell us?
Why is the lag time important for flood prediction?

explain.say: Today we are looking at how rivers respond to rain.
Rainfall is a key input that feeds the river system.
Outputs include water leaving the system, like evaporation.
Lag time is the delay between rain and peak flow.

draw.text: Lag time: Delay to peak flow

explain.say: A steep slope usually means a shorter lag time.
In real life, flash floods show a very short lag time.

faq.a: It is the entire area of land where all surface water drains to a single river or body of water. This area determines the river's flow patterns.
asks: What area drains into a river?

faq.q: How does rainfall affect the hydrograph?
faq.a: Increased rainfall generally leads to higher inputs, causing the peak flow on the hydrograph to rise. This shows more water entering the river.
asks: Does more rain mean higher river levels?
What causes the peak flow on a graph?

faq.q: What does 'lag time' mean in this context?
faq.a: Lag time is the time interval between the peak rainfall and the peak river flow. It shows how long it takes for the water to travel through the basin.
asks: What is the delay between rain and river peak?
How long does it take for runoff to peak?

faq.q: Can the land type affect the lag time?
faq.a: Yes, impermeable surfaces like concrete increase runoff speed, often decreasing the lag time. Porous soil allows water to soak in, increasing lag time.
asks: Does soil type matter for lag time?
How does ground cover affect river response?

faq.q: What are the main inputs and outputs?
faq.a: Inputs are primarily rainfall and surface runoff. Outputs include stream flow leaving the basin and water lost through evapotranspiration.

facts: A drainage basin collects all water draining to one point.
The hydrograph plots river flow against time.
Lag time is the delay between peak rainfall and peak river flow.
Steeper slopes generally result in shorter lag times.

quiz.say: If rainfall suddenly stops, what feature would you expect to see on the hydrograph?

options.show: A gradual decline in flow rate
options.say: A gradual decline in flow rate

quiz.why: The river continues to flow slowly from groundwater reserves after the rain stops.

wrong.0: Flow cannot increase if the input source (rain) has stopped.
wrong.2: This suggests all water leaves instantly, which is physically impossible.
wrong.3: A vertical line implies instantaneous removal of all water.

quiz.say: What factor generally causes a longer lag time?

options.show: A basin with highly porous soil
options.say: A basin with highly porous soil

quiz.why: Porous soil allows water to soak in and move slowly, delaying the peak flow.

wrong.0: Impermeable rock prevents soaking, leading to fast runoff and short lag times.
wrong.1: High evaporation reduces overall water volume, but doesn't dictate the time delay.
wrong.3: Steep gradients cause water to rush quickly, shortening the lag time.

quiz.say: If the river flow peaks much later than the rainfall peak, what is likely true about the basin?

options.show: It has a very steep gradient
options.say: It has a very steep gradient

options.show: It has very little surface runoff
options.say: It has very little surface runoff

options.show: It is located in a mountainous region
options.say: It is located in a mountainous region

options.show: It has a large area of permeable ground
options.say: It has a large area of permeable ground

quiz.why: Permeable ground absorbs water slowly, releasing it gradually over a longer period.

wrong.0: A steep gradient causes fast runoff, leading to a short lag time.
wrong.1: Low surface runoff does not necessarily mean a delayed peak; it could mean low overall flow.
wrong.2: Mountainous regions often have steep slopes, resulting in quick runoff.
